source.title: Linearly Constrained Weights: Reducing Activation Shift for Faster Training of Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. It includes figure descriptions and tables; some plotted training results have no exact values in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training curves and compares methods that alter activation shift or initialization, bearing on training convergence and trainability. It does not reproduce the claim's specified experiments.
record.gate_note: Training loss and accuracy curves are reported for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The training curves in Figures 5 and 6 are plotted without exact values in the text. The convolutional model table reports test metrics, which do not measure the claim's training-error outcome and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The VGG19 experiments measure training classification accuracy on CIFAR-100, bearing on V1. The sigmoid MLP experiments also compare training curves with and without BN for otherwise corresponding LCW, SL, WN, CWN and SN models, bearing on V6 in a new setting. The supplied text does not preserve the plotted curves well enough to determine either outcome.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors attribute faster sigmoid-MLP training to reduced activation shift and alleviated vanishing gradients, report improved generalization when LCW is combined with BN, and find a smaller benefit in ResNet18. These results concern the combined constraint and initialization recipe, rather than initialization alone.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes linearly constrained weights and compares them with normalization and weight methods. It does not reproduce the original sources' training recipes for the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported convergence and trainability differ across LCW, BN, SL, WN, CWN and SN; WN and SN alone did not proceed in the 50-layer sigmoid MLP experiments. The authors report little training-curve difference for ResNet18 with and without LCW.

fits_no_version.finding: LCW gives faster convergence and better training scores in 50-layer sigmoid MLPs and accelerates VGG19 training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintaining zero-sum weight constraints with the prescribed initialization can accelerate training in these architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: With the same minibatch-based preactivation-variance initialization, a 20-layer sigmoid MLP has shrinking backward gradients with standard weights and preserved or slightly increasing gradient variance with LCW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving forward preactivation variance at initialization alone need not preserve backward gradients; persistent weight constraints can alter that relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: LCW improves some test metrics, while standalone LCW's faster MLP training does not improve test performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training acceleration from LCW and improvements in generalization are distinct and depend on architecture and combination with BN.

record.problems: Training outcomes are primarily figures without exact numerical training-error values or uncertainty estimates. The study uses standard labels, not corrupted or random labels. Its main intervention combines an LCW constraint with a particular initialization procedure, limiting attribution to initialization alone.
record.rows_left_out: Rows R1–R23 include plotted training loss and accuracy for the CIFAR-10/100 MLP comparisons and CIFAR-100 VGG19 comparisons. No separate training rows were extracted for ResNet18 because the text states only that its training curves showed little difference with and without LCW, without exact values; this is not a direct test of the listed version outcomes.

untested.parts: Corrupted or random labels, controlled model-size comparisons, early stopping, and CIFAR-10 convolutional training-error outcomes are not reported. Test accuracy in Table 1 cannot establish training interpolation.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum frequency, or extra-neuron comparison.
No controlled depth comparison of plain and residual networks, longer-training degradation test, or special-initialization alternative.

No comparison isolating initialization's effect on learning speed or trainable depth. LCW combines initialization with a constraint maintained throughout training. Orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and extremely deep convolutional training are not tested.
No learning-rate stability threshold, curvature trajectory, catapult regime, or edge-of-stability experiment.
Higher-learning-rate tolerance and Fixup are not tested. All convolutional models already contain BN, so their comparisons do not isolate adding BN.

missing.what: Separate WN-alone and SN-alone rows for each CIFAR dataset. Section 6.1 explicitly reports that their training did not proceed; these failures are not outcomes of BN+WN or BN+SN. They provide relevant non-BN baselines for V6, although the combined-model curves remain unreadable.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is warranted from the readable evidence: Figure 6's axes do not establish near-zero training error, and Figure 5's legends and axes do not establish the direction of matched BN training-speed comparisons. The paper's qualitative claim that LCW trains faster cannot substitute for either outcome.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports CIFAR training curves for standard-label data, but does not state exact training classification errors. It does not test corrupted or random labels, smaller-model comparisons, early stopping, or the cited recipes.

Tests LCW and several normalization or weight methods, including a 50-hidden-layer sigmoid MLP; it does not compare orthogonal and Gaussian weights at equal variance or train a 10,000-layer plain convolutional network.
BN appears in combinations and in the base convolutional models, but the paper does not isolate adding BN against the same network without BN as a training-speed comparison.
